name: US dollar
summary: Dollar index near 102.1 early on 9 Nov, up 2.1% over three months and close to its 52-week high
state: The DXY dollar index was near 102.1 early on 9 Nov, up 2.1% over three months and just under its 52-week high of 102.6 (Yahoo Finance), inside the 5% Watch line and the 90–108 range. Dollar funding rates showed no strain in the latest data to 5–6 Nov (FRED).
for_you: A firmer dollar raises the local cost of dollar-priced imports such as oil and food, with the largest effect in emerging economies that borrow in dollars.
rubric_hit: DXY 3-month move +2.1% < 5% and level 102.1 inside 90–108: Normal
why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.
